items.name: Masoor Dal Tadka
steps: Rinse the red lentils; soak for 25 minutes and drain.
Simmer the pulse with turmeric and the tomato, diced in the measured water until tender enough to mash easily.
Warm the ghee separately; let the cumin crackle, then stir in the ginger.
Fold the tempering into the cooked dal, add the rock salt, and simmer uncovered for five minutes.
Adjust to a ladleable consistency by stirring well, then rest covered briefly before serving.
items.guidance: Masoor Dal Tadka balances a thoroughly cooked pulse with a restrained aromatic tempering. Vata: serve moist with ghee. Pitta: reduce ginger and use coriander seed. Kapha: reduce fat and add black pepper if suitable.

Rest covered for two minutes and serve warm.

items.name: Light Tomato Rasam
steps: Rinse the toor dal and simmer it in part of the water until soft; whisk it into a thin suspension.
Crush the cumin and black pepper coarsely, keeping the mixture textured rather than powdered.
Add the tamarind, ripe tomato, chopped, fresh cilantro, turmeric, salt, and remaining water; simmer until the raw sour aroma softens.
Stir in the dal liquid and heat only until the surface becomes foamy, without a prolonged hard boil.
Warm the ghee, pop the mustard seeds, and crisp the curry leaves; pour this tempering over the rasam before serving.
items.guidance: Light Tomato Rasam is a thin, sour-spiced broth intended for a modest portion. Vata: pair with soft rice and extra ghee. Pitta: reduce pepper and tamarind. Kapha: use the full pepper measure and little added fat.

items.name: Classic Mixed Vegetable Sambar
steps: Rinse and soak the toor dal for 25 minutes, then simmer it with turmeric until collapsing-soft.
Toast the coriander, cumin, and fenugreek gently; cool and grind them to a coarse sambar spice.
Cook the carrot, diced and green beans, cut and pumpkin, diced in the tamarind water until just tender.
Whisk the dal, combine it with the vegetables and ground spice, add salt, and simmer for eight minutes.
Warm the ghee, pop the mustard seeds, and crisp the curry leaves; fold this tempering through and serve while the vegetables still hold their shape.
